sections.title: Application
sections.body: These rules apply to all standing and ad hoc committees unless superseded by committee-specific rules adopted by the Assembly or referendum. Individual committees may adopt additional procedural rules by majority vote of their members, provided they do not conflict with these rules.
sections.rationale: Provides baseline governance for committees while allowing flexibility for specific committee needs.

sections.title: Authority
sections.body: Committee rules may be amended by Assembly vote (2/3 majority) or by referendum of the full membership. Committees may not alter their own governing rules, only internal procedures.
sections.rationale: Prevents committees from changing their own voting thresholds or fundamental procedures without broader oversight.

sections.title: Quorum
sections.body: A quorum of a simple majority (more than half) of seated committee members must be present for any vote to proceed. Votes taken without quorum are void.
sections.rationale: Lower quorum than Assembly reflects the smaller size and more focused scope of committee work. Still prevents minority decision-making.

sections.title: Simple Majority
sections.body: All committee decisions require a simple majority (more than half of votes cast) to pass, including: (1) recommendations to the Assembly, (2) internal procedures, (3) work product and reports, (4) requests for resources or information.
sections.rationale: Committees are advisory and investigative bodies. Their recommendations go to the Assembly for final approval, so simple majority is appropriate for committee work.

sections.title: Unanimous Recommendations
sections.body: When a committee passes a recommendation by unanimous vote, it shall be noted as such in the committee report. The Assembly may choose to expedite consideration of unanimous committee recommendations.
sections.rationale: Recognizes when committee work has achieved full consensus, signaling strong support to the Assembly.

sections.title: Open Deliberation
sections.body: All committee meetings and deliberations shall be open to observation by any member of the society. Committees may not conduct business in closed session except when legally required for personnel, legal, or confidential matters.
sections.rationale: Transparency in committee work builds trust and allows members to observe governance in action.

sections.title: Deliberation Period
sections.body: Motions before a committee should generally be deliberated for at least 48 hours before a vote, unless the committee unanimously agrees to expedite. Emergency motions may bypass this requirement with a 2/3 vote.
sections.rationale: Ensures committee members have time to consider questions thoroughly, while allowing flexibility for urgent matters.

sections.title: Minority Reports
sections.body: If a motion passes by less than 2/3 majority, dissenting committee members may attach a minority report explaining their opposition. Minority reports shall accompany the committee recommendation to the Assembly.
sections.rationale: Preserves dissenting views and provides the Assembly with a fuller picture of committee deliberations.

sections.title: Term Limits
sections.body: Committee members serve terms as specified in their committee's charter. Standing committees typically use sortition with staggered terms. Ad hoc committees serve until their charge is complete or they are dissolved.
sections.rationale: Allows flexibility for different committee types while ensuring regular rotation of membership.

sections.title: Vacancies
sections.body: If a committee seat becomes vacant, it shall be filled according to the method specified in the committee's charter (typically by sortition draw or Assembly appointment).
sections.rationale: Maintains full committee capacity while respecting the original composition method.

sections.title: Chair Selection
sections.body: If a committee requires a chair, the chair shall be selected by lot among committee members, unless the committee's charter specifies otherwise. Chairs serve administrative functions and do not have additional voting power.
sections.rationale: Random selection prevents political maneuvering for leadership positions. Chairs are coordinators, not commanders.
